Story of the gods.

They survived humanity’s collapse.
Can they stop it happening again?

Created by Mike Rashid King
A human drama on a cosmic scale.

Meet the ten survivors ↓

01 / The premise

Humanity has
been here before.

Forty thousand years ago, human civilization reached the stars—and destroyed itself. Ten consciousnesses survived aboard a living Mothership. Returning to a younger humanity repeating the same mistakes, they must decide: guide it through the Great Filter, end it, or let it choose its own future.

40,000Years ago
10Surviving minds
01World at stake

02 / The characters

Ten minds.
Ten ways to see humanity.

To us, they would seem like gods.
To themselves, they are still human.
Each carries a different answer to what comes next.

01 / 10

Sovereignty / The sun

The One Above

The central figure of the ten, shaped by hardship, failure, and sacrifice. He carries immense power—and the burden of protecting humanity without taking away its freedom.

02 / 10

Abundance / The living world

Anacaona

The Golden Flower embodies abundance, love, and the living world. Her power is to nurture what civilization needs to survive, with flourishing at the heart of her vision.

03 / 10

Consciousness / The inner world

Bahar

Bahar explores awareness, perception, and the mystery of being alive. Among minds capable of crossing the cosmos, she turns attention to the universe within.

04 / 10

Wisdom / Equilibrium

Solomon

The Inevitable One is counselor, ambassador, and judge. He seeks equilibrium between chaos and order, grounding his authority in discernment and the difficult pursuit of justice.

05 / 10

Resonance / Music

RhiAna

RhiAna gives music, vibration, and healing a human form. Her language of resonance creates connection beyond speech and asks how different voices can find harmony.

06 / 10

Conquest / Unity

Al Nabarr

Al Nabarr embodies the tension between conquest and unity. His formidable presence confronts the moral cost of domination—and whether peace imposed by force can ever be freely chosen.

07 / 10

The moon / Cycles

Luna

Luna embodies lunar cycles: change, tides, reflection, and return. She sees the patterns that shape worlds, asking whether humanity can recognize its cycle before repeating it.

08 / 10

Chemistry / Healing

Arkem

The physician and chemist understands life through elements and reactions. His power can restore bodies, alter minds, and test the boundary between healing and transformation.

09 / 10

Honor / Guardianship

Meiyoshin

A disciplined warrior and guardian whose strength is guided by honor. His loyalties bring the conflict between duty, conscience, and protection into sharp focus.

10 / 10

Probability / Possibility

Kephra

Kephra embodies probability and the branching paths behind every choice. She brings uncertainty to extraordinary knowledge, keeping the future open to possibility.

03 / The art canon

Drawn human.
Real camera.

The project names its visual language The Sacred Seven: a mature illustrated universe with the weight of cinema. Cosmic scale meets intimate human feeling, giving the story a signature that is recognizable before a word is spoken.

↳

The hand stays visible.

Graphite, charcoal, ink, and visible crosshatching preserve the texture of drawing. The image carries the mark of the hand.

↳

Human faces carry history.

Extraordinary beings retain a recognizable human presence. Their faces, posture, and culturally specific designs keep power connected to lived experience.

↳

Scale makes room for silence.

Monumental compositions create the weight of cinema while leaving space for stillness. The universe is immense; its emotional center stays close.

A summary of the visual principles described on the project website.

04 / Why this world connects

The power is cosmic.
The stakes are human.

The premise

An ancient future.

Humanity’s greatest civilization lies in its forgotten past. Its survivors return to confront the same greed, division, and war that brought their world down.

The drama

Power without consensus.

Ten perspectives turn the fate of humanity into a conflict of values. Saving a civilization may mean taking away the freedom that makes it human.

The identity

A world with a signature.

Tactile drawing, cinematic composition, and human faces give the project a distinct visual presence, built around a cast with clear identities and meaningful tensions.

The question at the center of everything

If you could save humanity from itself, would you let it remain free?

An original universe by Mike Rashid King.
Let’s bring its next chapter to life.
